journals.name: 11 — Session 1: The Son Who Came Home

pages.name: Session Overview
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

5. Session One - The Son Who Came Home

Purpose: Let the players enjoy surviving Barovia before introducing the costs of coming home. Establish affection, the social order and Baldrik's changed circumstances. No compulsory combat.

Prepared actors: Edda, Heddra, Runa, Baldrik, Hadrik, Brynja, Odran, Dagnner. Props: A military death register, feast seating, the old shield. End question: Will Thorgrinn allow his return to be used as an endorsement?

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 1.1 - Beyond the last mist | 20 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

1.1 - Beyond the last mist | 20 minutes

Place and actors: A mountain road; the party only, plus any NPCs they actually rescued from Ravenloft.

Read: "The mist breaks. The cold has a clean edge to it. Pine trees move in a wind that does not whisper your names. On the road below, a work crew's hammers strike stone in a familiar rhythm. Above a distant watchtower hangs a white fist gripping an iron nail."

Thorgrinn recognizes the emblem automatically. Give each player one brief question: what proves this is different from Barovia, and what are they carrying forward? Do not describe the destruction of native Barovians beyond the actual finale's established outcome. The new arc does not retroactively decide who escaped.

Offer three approaches: walk to the Finger, send a scout or rest out of sight. None triggers an ambush. A passing road crew provides directions and water. The exact magical mechanism keeping the party together is proposed continuation fiction, not an additional curse. Preserve any different escape method established in the finale.

Exit: The Fifth Finger opens its outer gate. Thorgrinn sees the old rank markings he once knew.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 1.2 - Recognition at the Fifth Finger | 35 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

1.2 - Recognition at the Fifth Finger | 35 minutes

Actors: Edda, two ordinary guards, a courier and a stranded supply crew.

Edda initially treats the party as travellers. When Thorgrinn identifies himself, she remembers his company and asks how he survived. This is an opportunity for shared history, not a test that can revoke his identity. Baldrik's old message lists him dead. Companions, recognisable habits and volunteered memories persuade her that the register needs correction. She offers shelter immediately.

A damaged wagon winch blocks the supply yard. The group can repair it, shift the load, use magic or organize the crew. This optional three-progress work challenge introduces practical heroism without requiring a fight. Success restores a shipment: D +1. Failure causes delay, not injury or a lost welcome.

A courier carries the story to Kharad-Varr while the party rests. Reports describe returning Ironfist kin and travellers claiming to have defeated a vampire lord; officials learn the details through witnesses and evidence, not instant omniscience.

Exit: The party chooses what proof and message to send. Heddra receives news before the generals finish composing theirs.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 1.3 - The door that still opens | 40 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

1.3 - The door that still opens | 40 minutes

Actors: Heddra, Runa, neighbours and the party; Baldrik has been summoned but has not arrived.

The next day, Heddra meets them in Lowhearth before the official reception. Her first words are "Come inside." She asks before embracing Thorgrinn. She offers the same hospitality to every companion and lets JP establish what food, drink and physical comfort mean in his present body.

Runa is fascinated by Thorgrinn's construction, notices herself treating him as an engineering mystery and apologizes. A direct boundary is respected. Heddra's repaired home shows Baldrik's money has genuinely improved lives. Beneath the repairs, damp walls, ration marks and military allocation stamps reveal persistent inequality.

Invite JP to establish one harmless childhood detail: a game, a household saying or a familiar hiding place. Do not ask for new traumatic canon. Heddra kept a memorial token because she believed Baldrik's report. She did not knowingly erase Thorgrinn.

Clue: Runa's work sash bears the Ninth Sluice assignment. She says shortages are causing trouble below, without giving the entire conspiracy away.

Exit: The feast summons arrives, addressed to all five heroes.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 1.4 - A table above their station | 55 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

1.4 - A table above their station | 55 minutes

Actors: The three generals, Dagnner, Heddra, Runa, ordinary veterans and the party.

Make the celebration sincere. Veterans ask about tactics; craftspeople offer repairs; a singer gets an amusing detail wrong and invites correction. Each companion receives a personal toast based on deeds they choose to describe. Heddra is seated beside Thorgrinn, not humiliated at the door. Social tension appears through quiet astonishment that a low-ranked household occupies the high table.

Hadrik offers the party hospitality and Thorgrinn an honorary commission. He wants a public sentence supporting "the security of our mountain." Let characters ask what that means. The written commission can be inspected: it includes service obligations and restrictions on speaking for the clan. It is not a magical contract.

Brynja asks whether the heroes will inspect an attacked water installation. Odran asks how long they intend to remain. Dagnner recognizes them and carefully avoids discussing the Barovian bounty in front of the crowd.

Choices: Accept honour without commission, negotiate terms, accept knowingly or refuse. None cancels the feast. No poisoning or staged assault spoils the welcome.

Exit: Baldrik enters after the toasts. He is holding the old shield.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 1.5 - Two mismatched rivets | 40 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

1.5 - Two mismatched rivets | 40 minutes

Actors: Baldrik, Thorgrinn; companions may stay if invited.

Move to a quieter side chamber. Baldrik's first reaction is relief rather than disgust. He asks, "May I?" before touching Thorgrinn's shoulder. The familiar shield is real; his affection is real; neither settles the past.

Baldrik says he saw the body, believed Damian's promise might be desperation and did not know how to live with their unfinished conversation. If Damian is present, he asks why Thorgrinn's death was described as an inconvenience. Let Damian explain his actions and tone; do not adjudicate who loved Thorgrinn correctly.

Baldrik wants another chance but offers it in the language he knows: lodging, rank, armour and protection. He does not offer a complete confession yet. A private conversation cannot solve years of conduct. If Thorgrinn refuses contact, Baldrik leaves the shield nearby without demanding forgiveness and agrees to communicate through someone Thorgrinn chooses.

Exit: Before leaving, Baldrik quietly asks the group to inspect the Ninth Sluice. He knows its official description is incomplete, but has not admitted that.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 1.6 - The sealed dispatch | 25 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

1.6 - The sealed dispatch | 25 minutes

Actors: Baldrik, Dagnner, a wounded adult courier; the party can witness or receive the dispatch secondhand.

A genuine raid has struck a lift beyond the Ninth Sluice. Workers and soldiers are trapped. The courier saw orc shield-bearers and goblin engineers cutting pump lines; no one has yet verified why that particular installation was targeted.

Dagnner delivers Hadrik's order to classify the route as a combat zone. Baldrik initially agrees with securing it, then hesitates at a clause permitting summary detention of "supporting households." He does not yet refuse.

The party can request command, volunteer independently or decline official service while helping workers. All lead to the same location with different access and authority. A refusal to help at all is allowed: the attack continues, and survivors bring evidence into Session 2 rather than forcing the party to travel.

Close: Heddra asks Baldrik, "When they say households, do they mean kitchens like ours?" End on his answer or inability to answer.

Compression and record: Shorten the parade, not the homecoming or reunion. Record the commission terms, Thorgrinn's boundaries, any D increase and what Baldrik now knows about the resurrection.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: Session Overview
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

6. Session Two - The Price of Protection

Purpose: Show that the invasion is dangerous while exposing the difference between defending people and defending policy. The first major combat is an objective-based rescue, not an ancestry-based extermination.

Prepared actors: Baldrik, Brynja, Tovik, Brakk, Ketta and captured raiders. Maps: A lift approach and a 70-by-50-foot sluice gallery with three levels, service walkways and a control station. Milestone: Level 11 at the end.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 2.1 - What the wounded actually saw | 25 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

2.1 - What the wounded actually saw | 25 minutes

Actors: Tovik, two injured workers, Yrsa and the party.

Yrsa is treating survivors. One worker saw raiders cutting the military feed line, not the household pipes. Another saw Brakk strike a surrendered guard. Both are true. Tovik says earlier complaints about dying lower wells were filed as enemy propaganda.

Basic care, introductions and listening reveal this information without rolls. Medicine, investigation or relevant magic can distinguish blast injuries from weapon wounds and establish which gallery failed first. Better information gives advantage on the first relevant navigation check, not an otherwise unavailable route.

A missing adult shift is still below. Put their names on a small roster so the rescue is about people rather than tokens. Civilians are not bait for an inevitable atrocity.

Clue: E1 begins with the dated gauge sheet Tovik carries: the new diversion started before the first raid in the log.

Exit: Brynja offers a transport cage and soldiers to hold the upper approach. The party decides whether Baldrik accompanies them.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 2.2 - The order and its limits | 40 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

2.2 - The order and its limits | 40 minutes

Actors: Brynja, Baldrik, Hadrik's written orders; Dagnner if she is escorting them.

The official task is to restore the pump, free the shift and identify attackers. A separate clause authorizes clearing all occupied chambers below the installation. Baldrik initially calls it ordinary operational language. Brynja agrees to narrow the party's orders if they point out the lack of identified targets.

This scene establishes command boundaries. Persuasion may improve troop support or access to records; the heroes do not need permission to avoid harming noncombatants. Accepting a commission does not grant magical obedience. If the party refuses the mission, Brynja still permits a civilian rescue under a neutral banner.

Dagnner wants recovered equipment counted. Damian can spot that requisitions exceed the garrison's actual needs. Legna can question whether a declared combat zone removes obligations to captives. Bunch can ask who will feed the trapped shift afterward.

Exit: Provide a written rescue mandate or note their independent status. It will matter when Hadrik later describes their actions.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 2.3 - The broken descent | 35 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

2.3 - The broken descent | 35 minutes

Actors: Tovik as guide; trapped adult workers across a lift shaft.

A counterweight has jammed, leaving a cage forty feet below the landing. The walls contain maintenance ladders, anchor rings and a hand brake. Characters can fly, climb, bridge the gap, repair the brake or move the cage by strength and leverage. Describe these options rather than waiting for a single correct skill.

Run a three-progress work challenge only if the party's method remains uncertain. A setback means lost equipment, noise alerting raiders or a slower approach. A fall uses the campaign's normal falling rules and offers the usual opportunities for rescue; no cinematic automatic death.

Workers describe raiders taking pump tools and water filters. One also reports that Korga's captain spoke of opening the upper gates. This foreshadows genuine conquest alongside the grievance.

Choice: Send rescued workers back with soldiers, shelter them in a defensible bay or bring them onward. All are viable with suitable protection.

Exit: Steam obscures the contested gallery; the main pressure wheel is turning the wrong way.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 2.4 - Battle at the Ninth Sluice | 60 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

2.4 - Battle at the Ninth Sluice | 60 minutes

Actors: Brakk using the Tunnel Captain profile, two Orc Shock Troopers and two Goblin Sappers. Five allied soldiers hold the entry and are background support, not five additional full turns.

The raiders want the pump regulator and intend to flood the defenders' approach. They attack armed opponents and will take prisoners, but Brakk has ordered unacceptable risks to the trapped workers. At the end of round 5, the sabotaged gate opens unless disabled.

The party has three simultaneous objectives: keep attackers away from the workers, stop the gate and secure a route out. The gate needs three actions of successful DC 16 work using tools, Athletics with a lever, Arcana on its actuator, or equivalent magic. Breaking its exposed chain also works: AC 15, 35 HP. The mechanism is visible and explained before initiative.

Killing every raider is unnecessary. Sappers surrender when Brakk falls and they have a safe exit. Brakk can be captured, forced to retreat or convinced to withdraw by losing the regulator and his tactical position.

Outcome: A stable gate and rescued shift give D +1. If the gate opens, the party can still escape; D -1 represents damaged infrastructure, not mandatory civilian deaths.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 2.5 - People on the other side | 35 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

2.5 - People on the other side | 35 minutes

Actors: Ketta or another surviving sapper, freed workers, Baldrik if present.

A captured raider carries a clay filter and a family ration tally. They admit the attack, do not pretend Brakk's conduct was harmless, and describe wells failing after the diversion. The account corroborates E1 but cannot by itself prove Hadrik's intent.

Baldrik asks for the prisoners to be transferred to military custody. He is not allowed to execute them by narrative fiat. The party can secure written protections, escort them to Yrsa, arrange an exchange or leave them with an officer they trust. A demonstrated safe-custody policy, with care for both dwarven wounded and enemy captives, earns A +1.

This is the first deliberate echo of the thieves in Neverwinter. The point is whether Baldrik recognizes it. Do not command Thorgrinn to intervene or cast the scene as a replay with a predetermined speech.

Exit: A captive offers the Treaty Stair as a contact point. Their cooperation survives a failed persuasion roll if the party treats them as a person.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 2.6 - The signature | 20 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

2.6 - The signature | 20 minutes

Actors: Baldrik, Runa and the party, or a courier if Baldrik is absent.

Among the recovered papers is a reference to a prior inspection signed by Baldrik. Runa recognizes the installation code and visibly stills. She confirms that an original civilian-safety design existed. Baldrik says, "I inspected the district. I did not order this raid."

That answer is true and incomplete. Let questions continue. If he admits his false report here, record it and remove the later need to force the confession; his admission does not solve the general's case or the war.

The party returns with workers, prisoners or both. Their choices become the version of events other people hear, not a fabricated claim that they supported a massacre.

Close: Runa asks to meet away from the military workshops. Award the milestone after the rescue and its aftermath, regardless of whether every enemy died.

Compression and record: Merge scenes 2.1 and 2.2 if combat runs long. Record Brakk and Ketta's fates, custody protections, D/A changes and whether Baldrik admitted his report.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: Session Overview
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

7. Session Three - What We Signed

Purpose: Make the family complicit in different, human ways and give every companion useful investigative work. The truth is recoverable without a single fragile document or perfect skill roll.

Prepared actors: Runa, Heddra, Baldrik, Dagnner, Venn, Odran, Yrsa. Maps: Optional workshop and records annex. Evidence in reach: E2 and E3, with several corroborating witnesses.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 3.1 - Competing invitations | 20 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

3.1 - Competing invitations | 20 minutes

Actors: Messengers for the generals, Heddra and the party.

The group receives three invitations: Hadrik wants a public statement; Odran offers access to provisioning records; Runa requests a private workshop meeting. Heddra asks for dinner that evening with both brothers.

Let the players choose their order and divide tasks if they wish. Present all three locations and their purposes. Do not run an unseen deadline that destroys the unvisited lead. Venn mentions that archive transfer is due tomorrow, providing a fair warning about delay.

Hadrik's requested wording says the heroes found "unprovoked aggression." They can amend, refuse or publicly contradict it. He does not get to quote words they never said; misleading publicity can be challenged with witnesses to the actual toast.

Exit: Establish who handles contracts, engineering and witness support. Spotlight is distributed by choice, not by restricting information to a designated character.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 3.2 - Three routes to the same lie | 60 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

3.2 - Three routes to the same lie | 60 minutes

Actors: Odran and Venn in the records office; Runa at the workshop; Yrsa and workers at the infirmary.

Run three short investigative scenes, returning to the whole table regularly. The accounts show military foundry output increasing as household supply falls (E2). The workshop contains an unused relief-valve specification that would have reduced the danger. The infirmary has dated records of contaminated water injuries predating the raids.

All basic facts are discoverable through access and sensible examination. DC 16 checks reveal extra advantages: an authenticated duplicate, a repair method, or a witness willing to testify publicly. On failure, the information still arrives but an official hears about the inquiry, or the witness asks for protection before attending.

Odran is willing to release accounts because he believes they justify the policy. He is disturbed by concealed maintenance costs. Do not turn every official into a liar.

Choice: The party can fund or organize an immediate repair crew. With Runa's cooperation and a practical supply plan, this earns D +1 once; simply buying influence does not.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 3.3 - Runa's commission | 35 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

3.3 - Runa's commission | 35 minutes

Actors: Runa, Thorgrinn and any interested companions.

Runa admits she noticed the bypass and kept quiet because her commission paid for the household's repairs. She has not knowingly designed a weapon against civilians. She offers her original notes and asks the party not to tell Heddra before she can do so herself.

That request creates a family choice, not a morality test. They can grant her a deadline, insist on immediate disclosure, bring Heddra in gently or leave Runa to decide. If they shame her, she may refuse public testimony but still supply calculations needed to save the district. No essential route disappears because the players were brusque.

Runa can assess Thorgrinn's body only if invited. She can discuss repair, craftsmanship and autonomy; she cannot identify a previously unknown control switch or guarantee flesh restoration. She explicitly says the pressure network has no need for a living soul.

Exit: She identifies the archive file containing Baldrik's inspection and gives a duplicate reference to Dagnner's receipts.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 3.4 - The record that survives | 45 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

3.4 - The record that survives | 45 minutes

Actors: Venn, Dagnner, two Shield Wardens and four ordinary Troopers if contested access becomes violent.

The party seeks E3. Legal access, negotiation with Dagnner, a discreet burglary, an official order from Odran or direct magical retrieval can all work. The archive has real locks and guards, not blanket antimagic.

E3 records Baldrik classifying inhabited lower galleries as military support territory after acknowledging food stores and civilian workshops. The signed appendix is the damaging part. It is not a forged signature. Dagnner has a duplicate; Venn can testify to filing it.

If Hadrik learns of the retrieval, he orders the file transferred, not spontaneously burned. Opposing guards attempt detention and protecting records. A fight is optional; they retreat or surrender rather than die for a cabinet. If the party loses access, Dagnner offers her duplicate for protection of her soldiers' wages and immunity only for truthful testimony, not for every offence.

Exit: The party has either the report, a credible description and witness, or Baldrik's earlier admission. Any supports the dinner scene.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 3.5 - Dinner with the missing places filled | 35 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

3.5 - Dinner with the missing places filled | 35 minutes

Actors: Heddra, Runa, Baldrik and the party.

Heddra serves a simple family meal and adjusts hospitality to the guests' actual bodies and preferences. No attack interrupts it. This is the emotional centre of the first half.

Baldrik first argues that the classification secured protection for the hold. Confronted with the actual text or people affected, he admits he knew families were there. Heddra admits accepting his money. Runa discloses her silence if she has agreed to do so. These admissions are different degrees of responsibility; do not flatten them into equal guilt.

Baldrik's central line is: "I thought if I stayed useful long enough, I would finally be the one who decided where the line was."

Then stop talking. Give Thorgrinn and the companions space. Baldrik may hear that the party restrained Thorgrinn during the sword curse without abandoning him. This can challenge his beliefs; it does not excuse his report or equate involuntary compulsion with deliberate policy.

Exit: Heddra will host displaced adults regardless of family disagreement. Practical support for her shelter and safe supplies earns A +1.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 3.6 - An answer under seal | 20 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

3.6 - An answer under seal | 20 minutes

Actors: A council messenger and, separately, a Cinder-Tusk contact.

The council summons the party to the public Roll of Service in two days. Hadrik intends to make Thorgrinn's new commission the centrepiece. He may also seek to question how the death register was corrected, but the document frames service obligations, not proof that a mechanical person deserves rights.

A second message offers a meeting at the Treaty Stair on the next day. It carries an old compact seal matching the sluice's stonework. The messenger seeks a witnessed truce, not a promise of surrender.

The party can make either message public, take soldiers, send an emissary or refuse the parley. Refusal changes Session 4 to reconnaissance and a rescue along the same route; Urzha can approach them there with witnesses rather than the GM forcing attendance.

Close: Baldrik asks whether Thorgrinn will speak with him before choosing whose banner to carry.

Compression and record: Reduce each investigation stop to one discovery, not the dinner. Record E2/E3, Runa's testimony, Baldrik's admission and who knows about the proposed parley.

◆ ◈ ◆

journals.name: 14 — Session 4: The Other Side of the Wall

pages.name: Session Overview
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

8. Session Four - The Other Side of the Wall

Purpose: Make peace possible but not easy. Establish the Cinder-Tusk as an organized society, identify Korga's expansionism, and give Baldrik a concrete chance to act differently.

Prepared actors: Urzha, Skrik, Ketta or another envoy, Baldrik, a Korga loyalist captain. Maps: Treaty Stair and a narrow pump bridge. Evidence: E4 and further proof for R1/R4.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 4.1 - A passage with witnesses | 20 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

4.1 - A passage with witnesses | 20 minutes

Actors: Brynja or a patrol officer, the party and any chosen escort.

At the border checkpoint, the heroes can obtain a limited truce banner, travel as independent envoys or approach unseen. Brynja asks for a report on actual troop positions. She does not demand sabotage of the negotiation.

Baldrik requests to accompany them. Accepting him gives access to military signals but alarms the Cinder-Tusk because his name appears on the classification report. Leaving him behind makes the meeting easier but postpones his public choice. Both are legitimate.

Any weapons arrangement is mutual and negotiated. Do not force the party to surrender signature items to reach the plot. A truce can instead establish distances, visible hands and agreed guards. Respect invisibility and scouting while letting discovered deception affect trust normally.

Exit: The party descends past dwarven markings that have been maintained beside newer goblin and orc engineering marks. The mountain is lived in, not an empty dungeon.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 4.2 - What the raid was supposed to retrieve | 30 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

4.2 - What the raid was supposed to retrieve | 30 minutes

Actors: Urzha's escort, wounded Cinder-Tusk adults, dwarven prisoners if captured earlier.

Before the council, show a filter station serving displaced households. Its supplies include tools taken at the Ninth Sluice. Urzha acknowledges this directly and offers to return nonessential property through an exchange. She will not apologize for needing water, but condemns Brakk's attack on a surrendered guard.

If the party protected captives in Session 2, their testimony opens the meeting without a trust check. If captives were mistreated, Urzha requires neutral witnesses and a specific safety commitment. She still has a reason to negotiate: a worse war will harm her people.

Skrik points out that opening only the upper feed will not restore the lower wells. The paired systems must be stabilized together. This is useful engineering information, not a demand that the party accept his politics.

Exit: Present the clan's copy of E4. The old compact names water obligations and shared access, not ownership of the entire mountain by either side.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 4.3 - The terms neither side likes | 40 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

4.3 - The terms neither side likes | 40 minutes

Actors: Urzha, Skrik, the party; Baldrik if invited.

Urzha requests restored water, return of prisoners, an inhabited boundary and witnessed accountability for attacks on civilians. In exchange she can arrange safe passage, technical assistance and opposition to Korga's conquest. She cannot honestly promise that every armed clan member will obey her.

Skrik admits his sabotage injured dwarven workers. He offers repair work and testimony, not a claim of perfect innocence. This makes reciprocal accountability possible.

Negotiations produce concrete commitments rather than an abstract persuasion score. A limited, witnessed agreement covering water and prisoners earns A +1. A broad permanent peace can be drafted, but the council and enough clan leaders must endorse it later. Diplomacy is not rendered worthless because Korga remains active.

Baldrik may apologize for the report. Urzha asks what he will do differently, not whether he feels sorry. A public promise to stop collective punishment creates a standard against which his next action will be judged.

Exit: Scouts report that a Korga loyalist team is moving to rupture the shared pump bridge.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 4.4 - The bridge both peoples need | 65 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

4.4 - The bridge both peoples need | 65 minutes

Actors: A Tunnel Captain, two Orc Shock Troopers, two Goblin Sappers; Skrik and Runa if present can advise but do not solve the encounter offscreen.

Korga's loyalists intend to destroy the connecting pump so the clan cannot accept a partial settlement. They also expect the resulting surge to damage the dwarf positions. The plan has military logic and unacceptable civilian costs. It is not Hadrik secretly directing their every action.

Use a 90-foot bridge with two raised valve platforms. Three charges are visible, each requiring one action and a DC 16 tool or Arcana check to disarm; a careful magical solution may replace the check. A failed attempt reveals a safer method but consumes the action. At the end of round 4 any remaining charge ruptures its section. Characters receive clear warning through sparking fuses and Skrik's shouted count.

The party can disable charges, drive off the captain, negotiate his withdrawal by showing his endangered supply route, or abandon the bridge and evacuate. Saving the main flow gives D +1. Losing it changes travel and supplies, not an unavoidable on-screen civilian massacre.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 4.5 - A familiar sentence | 40 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

4.5 - A familiar sentence | 40 minutes

Actors: Captured saboteurs, Baldrik or an Ironfist officer, Urzha and the party.

Afterward, a military officer demands that captive saboteurs be executed as a warning. The captured captain is genuinely culpable; some of the sappers did not know the bridge supplied their own displaced households. Evidence, role and responsibility matter individually.

If Baldrik is present, let him make a choice informed by earlier scenes. With his admission and a clear alternative custody plan, he can publicly refuse the unlawful summary order: "We are taking them in alive. That is the order you will obey." Record the second accountability event only if he actually takes this risk. If he defers, the party can still stop the execution; he has failed a moral opportunity, not become magically irredeemable.

If Baldrik is absent, send him the signed custody order and allow him to endorse or countermand it before the next hearing. His decision becomes public through his own troops.

Exit: Urzha offers guides and warns of Korga's larger offensive. The party has seen both grounds for negotiation and grounds for defence.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 4.6 - A treaty is an object, not a feeling | 20 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

4.6 - A treaty is an object, not a feeling | 20 minutes

Actors: The surviving negotiators and party.

Write down agreed terms: who controls each valve, how prisoners are exchanged, who witnesses compliance, and what happens when either side breaches it. Do not settle the entire caste system in this scene.

A clan scout produces a copied assault order targeting the upper reservoir, corroborating R4. The invasion timetable is real even if the parley succeeds. Urzha can bring some households and engineers out of Korga's coalition; she cannot dissolve an army by declaration.

The party chooses which evidence and negotiators to take to the public hearing. Escorting Urzha openly has political consequences but makes firsthand testimony possible. A remote signed statement is less dramatic but still useful evidence.

Close: Above the Treaty Stair, the council's herald announces Thorgrinn's proposed commission and invites the entire hold to witness it.

Compression and record: Shorten travel and combine terms with the closing scene. Record E4, actual treaty terms, the bridge's condition and Baldrik's public action or refusal.

◆ ◈ ◆

journals.name: 15 — Session 5: The Living and the Loyal

pages.name: Session Overview
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

9. Session Five - The Living and the Loyal

Purpose: Turn private discoveries into public consequences. The party can win this political confrontation. Hadrik is not guaranteed escape, immunity or a later boss appearance.

Prepared actors: All three generals, Baldrik, Heddra, Runa, Dagnner, Yrsa, Venn, workers and any Cinder-Tusk witnesses. Map: Hammerhall with a public gallery and four ordinary exits. Milestone: Level 12 at the end.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 5.1 - Read the commission before the ceremony | 20 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

5.1 - Read the commission before the ceremony | 20 minutes

Actors: Odran's clerk, the party, chosen advocates.

Give the party the actual text of Thorgrinn's proposed commission. It offers salary, housing and authority but obligates its holder to obey lawful military orders, disclose operational research undertaken with military resources, and speak only within an assigned remit. Hadrik wants to stretch those clauses to cover Thorgrinn's body. That interpretation is disputed, not a fact of the setting.

The correction to the death register can be separated from enlistment. Yrsa and Venn explicitly say so. The party can insist on separate proceedings, strike clauses, decline service or sign with full knowledge. No signature is required for continued personhood or access to the plot.

Players choose an opening speaker, witnesses and which evidence to disclose. Do not require polished player oratory: a clear account of the character's argument is enough.

Exit: The public doors open. Heddra sits with the workers rather than hiding in the family box.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 5.2 - The public roll | 55 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

5.2 - The public roll | 55 minutes

Actors: The council and witnesses.

Hadrik praises Thorgrinn first. He argues that strong leadership, restored military discipline and the heroes' example can end the crisis. His public case is attractive because the threat is real. He then calls on Thorgrinn to endorse the operation.

Let the party set its case. E1 plus Runa's testimony establishes the diversion's sequence. E2 challenges its claimed necessity. E3 establishes Baldrik's responsibility. E4 proves a compact existed. Different evidence supports different claims; no one paper automatically proves everything.

Brynja asks what alternative keeps the hold defended. Odran asks what supplies and payments honour the proposed agreement. Hadrik asks whether the heroes will accept responsibility if diplomacy fails. These are policy questions, not magical truth tests.

Run three issue rounds: cause of the crisis, treatment of civilians, and immediate command. Evidence establishes facts automatically when authenticated. A DC 16 social check can win a narrower concession, move an uncertain witness or reduce the conditions attached to a vote. It cannot delete proof on a failure.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 5.3 - Baldrik on the record | 30 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

5.3 - Baldrik on the record | 30 minutes

Actors: Baldrik, Heddra, Runa and the party.

Baldrik is asked whether he knew the lower districts were inhabited. If he previously confessed, this is the test of saying it publicly. If he has not, E3 confronts him directly. His options are to admit, evade or lie; do not predetermine redemption.

When he admits responsibility, he says: "I signed it. They were not all fighters. I knew that. I told myself being the officer would let me protect them later." He does not claim that his love for Thorgrinn absolves him.

Hadrik tries to isolate him as the sole negligent inspector. Runa's design notes and the general's authorization rebut that without making Baldrik innocent. Heddra can acknowledge her own silence while insisting civilians should not bear the punishment for it.

If Baldrik submits the report and accepts a formal inquiry, record his third accountability event. The refusal-of-order event still matters separately; testimony does not retroactively manufacture it.

Exit: Give Thorgrinn the choice to speak for him, against him, for a fair process, or not at all.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 5.4 - Three generals, actual consequences | 35 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

5.4 - Three generals, actual consequences | 35 minutes

Actors: Hadrik, Brynja, Odran, the party and their supporters.

The council votes on a limited resolution: suspend collective-clearance operations, protect prisoners and establish independent oversight of the sluice. Brynja supports it with credible risk evidence and a defence plan. Odran supports it with authenticated compact or accounts and a workable provisioning arrangement. Their stated conditions can be satisfied in more than one way.

A successful resolution gives D +1 through unified lawful command. It can also suspend Hadrik or authorize his detention if the evidence establishes deliberate concealment. Resolve any attempted flight or resistance normally. He does not disappear between scenes. His guards may obey the council, surrender or protect an exit; use the ordinary combat profiles if needed.

If the vote fails, the party retains its evidence and allies. Hadrik announces emergency command. The resulting division costs D -1, but Brynja can issue a humanitarian access order and the party can publish the evidence or organize a protective escort. Do not automatically imprison the PCs.

Exit: The result determines who can issue orders in the coming war, not whether the next chapters exist.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 5.5 - What Last Bastion means | 55 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

5.5 - What Last Bastion means | 55 minutes

Actors: Runa, Skrik if present, Yrsa, maintenance workers and whoever controls the council.

A scheduled pressure test begins at a lower exchange. It was authorized before the hearing; introduce its notice in scene 5.1. If the party already suspended it effectively, honour that: run a controlled inspection instead of causing the accident anyway.

During an unsuspended test, relief vents open toward Lowhearth. The party must evacuate a workshop bay, close a manual intake and protect the control desk. Use three progress for the intake and two for evacuation, with five exploration rounds of coordinated actions. Spells and directing workers count when appropriate. Failure means ruined homes, injuries and D -1; assign deaths only through the table's established stakes and avoid gratuitous civilian suffering.

A controlled inspection obtains the same discovery with less danger: E5, the sealed Last Bastion order, and evidence that the operating diagram omits occupied lower galleries. Runa can now begin E6. The purge is no longer hypothetical.

Exit: The party learns that merely cancelling a written order is not enough; the armed physical reversal latch must be secured at the Heartworks, unless they have already done so.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 5.6 - Who gives the next order? | 20 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

5.6 - Who gives the next order? | 20 minutes

Actors: The surviving authorities, Baldrik, Urzha's messenger and the party.

Korga's forces are assembling for the upper reservoir assault. This is independent of Hadrik's legal fate. Urzha reports which households and engineers will stand aside or cooperate under the negotiated terms.

The party chooses a public mandate: lawful envoys under Brynja, a civilian protection coalition, independent emergency assistance or continued military service on negotiated terms. None requires Thorgrinn to become clan ruler.

If Hadrik remains free, he issues instructions to preserve Last Bastion and withdraws only through a route the players genuinely fail or choose not to block. If detained, his signed orders and the physical latch remain recoverable evidence, not an excuse to make a subordinate equally powerful.

Close: Baldrik removes his ceremonial cloak before speaking to Thorgrinn. Whether he offers his captain's badge, keeps it to protect his soldiers or doubles down depends on his choices so far.

Compression and record: Merge the first two issue rounds if needed. Preserve the family testimony. Record the vote, Hadrik's actual location, command authority, E5, casualties or damage, and the level milestone.

◆ ◈ ◆

journals.name: 16 — Session 6: A Shield Wall Has Two Sides

pages.name: Session Overview
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

10. Session Six - A Shield Wall Has Two Sides

Purpose: Convert agreements into trust through shared danger. Recover the physical means to halt Last Bastion and force Baldrik to choose what his authority is for.

Prepared actors: Baldrik, Dagnner, Runa, Skrik, Urzha, Brynja, stranded Vanguard soldiers and Korga loyalists. Maps: Cinder Warrens evacuation route and a 60-by-80-foot redoubt with gate, stores and records room.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 6.1 - The war table, not the throne | 30 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

6.1 - The war table, not the throne | 30 minutes

Actors: Brynja or the party's chosen command partners, Urzha, Runa and Skrik.

Present the operational facts: Korga can reach the upper works tomorrow; civilian movement must finish before then; the physical reversal latch is reachable through the Vanguard Redoubt or a service route. The original manual and a release key are stored at the redoubt. Hadrik's captured keys or engineering magic can provide alternatives.

The party chooses its approach. A lawful mandate gets access to some soldiers; an independent coalition gains service routes; a negotiated Cinder-Tusk compact provides local guides. None is universally best.

Runa and Skrik compare drawings and complete E6: the purge will damage both populations. They explain this in front of witnesses. Their collaboration is earned by the party's earlier work, not a sudden friendship that removes accountability.

Exit: State the timetable and rest opportunities clearly. The party can travel together, send allies on a separate evacuation or use transport magic to do both.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 6.2 - The homes beyond the military map | 40 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

6.2 - The homes beyond the military map | 40 minutes

Actors: Urzha, displaced adults, Cinder-Tusk guides and the party.

The route passes an inhabited cavern damaged by bad water and the clan's own military requisitions. Some residents welcome help; others distrust anyone wearing Ironfist colours. A dwarf prisoner working beside a goblin mechanic provides evidence that individuals have already crossed the supposed absolute divide.

The party can escort civilians along the Treaty Stair, arrange a protected passage through Lowhearth or shelter them in a neutral service cavern. Any viable, consent-based evacuation plan implemented with local representatives earns A +1. They cannot simply order everyone to abandon ancestral homes and call it peace.

If the party has rejected diplomacy, this becomes a chance to protect noncombatants during reconnaissance. Korga's aggression does not make the occupants automatic combatants.

Clue: Residents identify the main invasion path and a service route to the redoubt. No one must betray family in exchange for rescue.

Exit: A signal lamp from the redoubt reports wounded soldiers and a disputed withdrawal order.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 6.3 - An exchange with names | 30 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

6.3 - An exchange with names | 30 minutes

Actors: Urzha, Dagnner, prisoners from both sides, Baldrik if present.

Arrange the promised prisoner exchange. Name two adults on each side and give each a simple concern: an untreated wound, a missing wage packet, news for a household or fear of prosecution. Captives accused of specific crimes can be transferred into witnessed custody rather than released unconditionally.

Dagnner will provide the duplicate Last Bastion dispatch and stores inventory if her soldiers receive safe passage and lawful wages. She cannot demand immunity for unidentified future offences. The party may negotiate testimony protection but should record its limits.

If prisoners died or escaped earlier, replace the exchange with transfer of remains, witness statements and safe passage for the living. Do not resurrect NPCs solely to restore a planned beat.

Exit: Dagnner warns that the redoubt's officers have conflicting orders. A ceasefire may open the gate. Forcing it is possible, but troops will not all interpret the same banner identically.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 6.4 - The Vanguard Redoubt | 60 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

6.4 - The Vanguard Redoubt | 60 minutes

Actors: Two Shield Wardens, six ordinary Troopers, a loyalist Tunnel Captain with two Shock Troopers on the outer approach, plus wounded soldiers as background.

This is a three-sided tactical situation, not one huge combined encounter. The redoubt's defenders fear betrayal, Korga's force wants the stores, and the party needs the manual, key and safe withdrawal of the wounded. Resolve negotiation first. Authentic orders, Baldrik's authority, evidence of the purge or Dagnner's signal can make the wardens allies.

If negotiation works, run a short defensive clash against the captain and two troopers, with friendly soldiers holding other entrances. If negotiation fails, the party can infiltrate, use the service route or fight the wardens while the outer threat pressures everyone. Never field both groups at full strength as an unannounced punishment.

The manual is in a reinforced desk: AC 17, 30 HP, or DC 16 tools. Its case protects the contents if broken. The key is held by the duty officer, who can surrender or bargain. Preserving stores and arranging withdrawal gives D +1; destroying the redoubt without an evacuation costs D -1.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 6.5 - The order he cannot postpone | 35 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

6.5 - The order he cannot postpone | 35 minutes

Actors: Baldrik, his remaining soldiers, Thorgrinn and the party.

Baldrik receives or is confronted with an order to close the safe passage before displaced Cinder-Tusk civilians finish crossing. The order protects the retreat tactically but abandons people the party has promised to protect. Offer a viable alternative: hold the flank, move the wounded first through another gate, negotiate a temporary standstill or use the party's magic.

This is not a forced choice between one brother and a hundred strangers. It is a choice about accepting risk and responsibility. If Baldrik orders protection of the civilians in front of his troops, record his refusal-of-unlawful-order event. If he still obeys the closure, the party can oppose him. A fight, resignation or arrest is possible, not compulsory.

Baldrik's earned line is: "I cannot undo the report. I can decide who gets through this gate."

If Baldrik is dead, absent or imprisoned, the scene belongs to his company and the party's interpretation of his legacy. Do not create an identical replacement brother.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 6.6 - The plan everyone can understand | 20 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

6.6 - The plan everyone can understand | 20 minutes

Actors: The party and the allies they actually retained.

Use the manual to explain the final system: a reservoir wheel, a relief channel and a reversal brake must be operated together. The Bastion maintenance engine guards its armed settings. A mechanical body is not required, and no soul sacrifice is part of the solution.

The party can attempt to disable the system now. If its route, time and actions permit success, let it succeed. Session 8 then becomes the settlement-and-aftermath version rather than inventing another engine. If they only secure the manual and route, they have reliable preparation for the later emergency.

Choose tomorrow's defence assignments and make arrangements for Heddra, prisoners and vulnerable workshops. Allow the scheduled long rest before the siege unless the party chooses another urgent objective.

Close: Thorgrinn may stand beside Baldrik at the watch post, leave him under guard, or walk away. Whichever happens, the two-rivet shield remains a reminder, not a command to reconcile.

Compression and record: Combine the exchange with the redoubt negotiation. Record custody, the manual and key, any early shutdown, D/A, Baldrik's public decision and the army's chain of command.

◆ ◈ ◆

journals.name: 17 — Session 7: The War Inside the Mountain

pages.name: Session Overview
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

11. Session Seven - The War Inside the Mountain

Purpose: Pay off preparation through an actual military confrontation. The party makes decisions at the points where a few extraordinary people can change a battle; do not simulate hundreds of independent turns.

Prepared actors: Korga, Brynja, Urzha, Runa, Skrik, Baldrik and Dagnner according to their survival and loyalties. Maps: Muster table, one chosen front, command bridge. Resources: Use the declared operational day; the party begins rested if it took the offered rest.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 7.1 - Three fronts, one party | 25 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

7.1 - Three fronts, one party | 25 minutes

Actors: The coalition's actual commanders.

Display three fronts: the upper gate protects food and access to the surface; the lower bridge protects evacuees; the pump galleries protect the water network. The party chooses one to handle directly and assigns allies to the others. A shield guardian, retained troop unit, dragon ally outside the hold or a creative magical defence can substantially improve an assignment.

Apply the published D/A consequences. D 0-1 means an unassigned position must fall back; ask which stores or ground to sacrifice after explaining the choices. D 2-3 holds both unassigned positions with damage. D 4-6 holds them and grants one reinforcement benefit: remove two ordinary enemies from the chosen encounter, recover one endangered objective, or provide two successful work actions during the operation.

A 2 supplies a safe civilian route. A 3-4 also brings Cinder-Tusk engineers and publicly undermines Korga's claim that cooperation is impossible.

Exit: The horns sound. The players know what their decisions are buying.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 7.2 - The cost of an order | 30 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

7.2 - The cost of an order | 30 minutes

Actors: Heddra coordinating shelter, a messenger from an unassigned front, the party's chosen allies.

Run a command scene before the first battle. A messenger reports an emerging problem on an unassigned front. The party can reassign an ally, spend material resources, personally change its objective or accept a manageable loss. Show the actual cost: food stores, access time, damaged buildings or a tougher retreat. Avoid an opaque choice that secretly means mass death.

Heddra asks for a line on the map marking where people can still walk safely. Bunch can coordinate signals; Damian can direct supplies or exploit enemy communications; Vesper and Legna can organize protection; Thorgrinn can advise on holding a line. Any character can take any role they justify.

If the party negotiates with Korga at this stage, he can hear terms. He needs to see both credible force and an alternative his people will accept; a ceasefire pauses attacks while talks occur rather than being automatically betrayed.

Exit: Play the selected front or the equivalent verification mission supporting a negotiated ceasefire.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 7.3 - The chosen front | 60 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

7.3 - The chosen front | 60 minutes

Choose one prepared encounter; the other two are resolved by assignments, not played as mandatory extra combats.

Upper Gate: Two Shock Troopers, two Sappers and a Tunnel Captain escort a battering engine. Stop three successful ram impacts before the end of round 5. The engine is AC 17, 80 HP; disabling its two exposed haul chains takes one DC 16 action each and removes one attack route. Teleporting or flying behind it is effective.

Lower Bridge: Two Shock Troopers and three Sappers attempt to cut the evacuation path. Keep a marked ten-foot corridor passable for four rounds; allied workers move the civilians. The heroes can reroute the crossing, create a magical bridge or negotiate withdrawal. They need not personally carry every person.

Pump Galleries: A Tunnel Captain and three Sappers occupy two controls. Secure both and gain four total work progress before round 5 to prevent damaging flow reversal. Existing water-control magic or the release key can provide an equivalent solution.

Enemy morale breaks when the captain falls or the main objective becomes impossible, unless a specific leader offers credible reinforcements. Victories are determined by outcomes, not corpse counts.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 7.4 - The shield between them | 25 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

7.4 - The shield between them | 25 minutes

Actors: Baldrik, Thorgrinn, selected companions and remaining Vanguard soldiers.

During a tactical pause, Baldrik offers his company to protect the party's approach to Korga. He does not demand that Thorgrinn return to the family unit or accept a rank. An accountable Baldrik asks, "Where do you need us?" A defensive Baldrik says, "Stay behind my shield," revealing that his instincts have not fully changed.

The party can accept his help, place him under another command, leave him guarding evacuees or keep him in custody. Each is mechanically viable. A retained competent company removes one ordinary guard from Korga's scene or ensures a retreat route, but does not defeat the boss for the players.

No falling bridge demands his scripted sacrifice. If the players choose a dangerous rear-guard action, resolve it with a stated task and normal chances of escape. Death is a consequence of play, not the price of forgiving him.

Exit: Scouts identify Korga at the command bridge directing the next assault.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 7.5 - Korga's last argument | 55 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

7.5 - Korga's last argument | 55 minutes

Actors: Korga and two Shock Troopers, reduced by applicable allies or earlier victories. Urzha can attend under a truce or relay terms.

At a broad bridge overlooking the reservoir, Korga argues that victory is the only guarantee his people will ever have. He admits the campaign now seeks the upper gates. He does not pretend a captured family ration book excuses every order.

There are three resolutions. Combat can kill, capture or drive him from command. A negotiated command challenge can settle his leadership if both sides agreed its terms beforehand; it is not a compulsory duel for Thorgrinn. A credible peace can remove his mandate: A at least 3, a witnessed water agreement, a real end to the purge, and enough military pressure or clan support that continuing costs him his command. Social checks can refine surrender terms, not replace those conditions.

In combat, use Korga's profile and the bridge's marked cover and side stairs. Do not collapse it without warning. At half HP he seeks a better position; at 40 HP with no supporters and a viable surrender offer, he can yield.

Exit: The assault ends or loses central coordination. Determine which troops surrender, retreat or remain for an orderly withdrawal.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 7.6 - Victory, and the pressure gauge | 20 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

7.6 - Victory, and the pressure gauge | 20 minutes

Actors: Runa, Skrik or another surviving engineer; the party.

If Last Bastion remains armed, siege damage and the already documented reversal latch begin driving pressure toward the purge configuration. This is the consequence foreshadowed in Sessions 5-6, not a secret new machine. Hadrik can deliberately accelerate it only if he is actually free and able to reach its controls.

Explain the four-hour horizon, the route and available short rest. The engineers present the same three stations already described. Killing Korga or Hadrik does not repair a pressurized network, but securing or disabling it earlier absolutely prevents this emergency.

If the party already made the system safe, reveal the good news instead. Session 8 opens with inspection, demobilization and settlement, with no fabricated final catastrophe. They have earned a quieter ending.

Close: The war horns fall silent. In the unsettled version, a deeper mechanical pulse continues under the stone. In the secure version, the first clean water returns to a lower public fountain.

Compression and record: Reduce command discussion before cutting the Korga resolution. Record all front outcomes, Korga's fate, Hadrik's actual status, resources remaining and whether the emergency still exists.

◆ ◈ ◆

journals.name: 18 — Session 8: What We Choose to Keep

pages.name: Session Overview
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

12. Session Eight - What We Choose to Keep

Purpose: Resolve the physical danger, political responsibility and family question separately. No single boss death repairs every relationship. No character must change body or accept leadership to complete the arc.

Prepared actors: The allies and antagonists actually alive, free and present. Map: A 90-by-70-foot Heartworks with three regulator platforms, central engine, walkways and two exits. Milestone: Level 13 at the conclusion.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 8.1 - Before the last door | 20 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

8.1 - Before the last door | 20 minutes

Actors: Thorgrinn, Baldrik if available, the party and engineers.

Allow a short rest inside the established four-hour preparation window, then a final conversation. Baldrik makes no request for instant absolution. If accountable, he tells Thorgrinn he will give evidence and accept judgement. If still evasive, he offers family loyalty in place of accountability; the difference should be obvious without a narrator declaring him redeemed or damned.

Runa offers Thorgrinn a choice of practical repairs or no intervention. She repeats that his body is not the key and his soul is not fuel. Heddra sends a simple message: "There is a place for all of you when this is over."

Players decide who goes into the Heartworks and who supports evacuation. Allies operate background routes, not the player characters' most important actions.

Secure-system alternative: Use this scene for a shared inspection that verifies the mountain is safe, followed by preparation for the public settlement.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 8.2 - The Heartworks opens | 30 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

8.2 - The Heartworks opens | 30 minutes

Actors: Runa and Skrik as advisers or their recovered notes; Hadrik only if his actual position permits.

Show the three stations before initiative: the reservoir wheel feeds the circuit; the relief channel safely releases pressure; the reversal brake locks the new arrangement. Each needs two progress. At a station, a character can spend an action on a DC 16 appropriate check, make a clearly applicable magical intervention, or use a prepared key for one automatic progress. Once a station has two progress, it stays set unless the party knowingly reverses it.

All three must be completed to stop the system. Tasks can be distributed in any order. A completed relief channel grants one extra round in the coming countdown. A 3-4 Accord engineering team starts one chosen station with one progress; the party must still secure the area and complete the work.

Hadrik, if present, offers to cancel the purge if allowed to retain command. This is leverage over controls, not Thorgrinn. Arrest, negotiation, surrender and immediate attack remain available.

Secure-system alternative: Demonstrate the functioning safeguards and authenticate E6 for the public record.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 8.3 - Last Bastion | 70 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

8.3 - Last Bastion | 70 minutes

Actors: Bastion Engine and, only if still free and present, Hadrik. Use the encounter adjustments in Appendix A; do not add a full-strength second boss merely because both survived.

The engine follows locked military instructions and attacks interference. It contains no captive soul. Explain that disabling or destroying it removes the physical guardian but does not by itself open the relief channel. Conversely, completing all three stations stops the purge and makes the engine stand down: combat is not mandatory to the finish.

The countdown begins at the end of the first combat round after the visible warning bell. Six rounds remain; completing relief adds one. At the end of each round, describe the next marked pressure stage. Successful work is never secretly erased. A full shutdown, a clearly effective major spell or a credible engineered alternative ends the threat.

If time expires, an initial rupture floods a lower industrial bay and closes one approach; it does not instantly kill both populations. The party has two additional rounds to open relief or evacuate through the two marked exits. A later shutdown can still save the hold, with major damage, displacement and a more difficult settlement. Telegraph those consequences before the last choice.

Secure-system alternative: Spend the equivalent time on two contested settlement issues chosen by the players, reconstruction decisions and a meaningful memorial scene. Do not insert a replacement villain.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 8.4 - The record nobody gets to edit | 35 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

8.4 - The record nobody gets to edit | 35 minutes

Actors: Brynja, Odran, Urzha, witnesses, the party and defendants who survived.

Hold a provisional public inquiry with independent witnesses. It is not a final trial for every wartime action. Establish immediate protections, custody and a dated future process. Hadrik's orders, Baldrik's report, Korga's attacks and Skrik's sabotage are assessed separately. Saving lives earns gratitude, not blanket immunity.

The party chooses what it advocates: civilian oversight of water, a limited boundary compact, review of military requisition powers, guaranteed hearings for prisoners, protected engineering access and reparations. The society cannot become egalitarian overnight because five adventurers made a speech. A signed, witnessed reform with officials and residents committed to enforcing it is a real victory.

Thorgrinn's death record is corrected independently of whether he takes a commission. Hadrik's attempt to treat his body as military research is rejected unless the party has consciously endorsed such a settlement; even then, ownership is a contested abuse, not narrator-certified truth.

Exit: Show who will actually do the work after the party leaves: named clerks, engineers, officers and civilian representatives.

◆ ◈ ◆

pages.name: 8.5 - Brothers, not a verdict | 35 minutes
pages.html:
◆ ◈ ◆

8.5 - Brothers, not a verdict | 35 minutes

Actors: Thorgrinn, Baldrik if alive, Heddra, Runa and companions as invited.

Return to the family table or the old training yard. The shield is present. Baldrik can offer restitution and honesty, ask for time, accept estrangement or cling to rank. Play the man produced by eight sessions, not the ending you hoped to get.

Thorgrinn may forgive, set conditions, refuse contact, retain affection without trust or ask his brother to help others rather than him. None forfeits the adventure's rewards. A reconciliation should name something concrete: testimony, surrendering command, rebuilding damaged homes or reporting to an independent inquiry. Death does not automatically wash away responsibility; a dead Baldrik leaves testimony, grief and choices about what story to tell.

Ask JP, "What do you want to keep, and what are you not willing to carry for him anymore?" Do not answer for him.

For bodily identity, the default ending is still mechanical. A trustworthy investigation into restoration can begin if Thorgrinn wants it, but the module invents neither his original body's location nor a guaranteed cure. Existing effective player magic is not blocked.

8.6 - The next morning | 25 minutes

Actors: Every surviving player character, with selected NPCs in short epilogue beats.

Give each player a final choice: a responsibility accepted, a relationship changed, a project funded, a possession left behind or a road they intend to take. Damian may negotiate a lasting supply agreement; Vesper may establish protected care; Legna may revise an oath; Bunch may help create a communal signal system. These are examples, not assigned endings.

Reward the group with an actual safe base, trusted craftspeople, reciprocal travel rights where negotiated, and payment or material support appropriate to their already substantial resources. Do not drown an already powerful party in another set of oversized weapons.

Optional family reward: the two-rivet shield becomes a consensual symbol, not compulsory property transferred from Baldrik. The mechanical reward in Appendix A can instead be placed on a new badge shared with the entire party.

Final image: clean water entering a lower cistern, a gate held open rather than shut, or two brothers standing at the same wall with room between them. Choose the image that matches their decisions.

Compression and record: Never sacrifice the final family conversation to extend a boss fight. Remove remaining ordinary enemies when their objectives collapse. Complete the milestone and close the eight-session arc here, without a compulsory ninth-session villain reveal.

Appendix A. Encounter profiles and table procedures

Scope and shared rules

These compact profiles are original homebrew scaffolding for this party, not official monster statistics or a claim of tested balance. They supply the numbers needed for the planned encounters. Use existing superior NPC sheets where available. Ability modifiers below run in the order Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma. Unlisted saves use the relevant ability modifier; unlisted skills do likewise. All ordinary combatants speak the languages reasonably established for them, can perceive their immediate battlefield and use normal movement, reactions, cover, grappling and concentration under your table's rules. Their ancestry does not give them unexplained immunity to player abilities.

All listed attacks use the stated attack bonus and deal the dice damage on a hit. A creature has one reaction each round. Legendary actions refresh at the start of its turn and occur at the end of another creature's turn, one option at a time. Recharge 5-6 means roll a d6 at the start of the creature's turn and regain the feature on 5 or 6. Use the party's established critical-hit rule. Morale guidelines are starting dispositions, not magical compulsion.

The strongest encounters assume five well-equipped PCs near the planned level. For four PCs, remove one supporting enemy and reduce a boss's HP by about 15 percent before initiative. For six PCs, add one ordinary support enemy or an exposed secondary objective rather than simply raising every AC. If the party's unusual equipment makes a fight easy, let it be easy; preserve strategic stakes through the stated objectives, not secret mid-fight HP inflation.

Ironfist Trooper

Medium combatant. AC 17; HP 32; speed 25 feet. Modifiers: +3, +0, +2, +0, +1, +0. Saves: Strength +6, Constitution +5. Perception: +4, passive 14.

Action - Multiattack: Two spear attacks, +6 to hit, reach 5 feet or range 20/60 feet; 1d8 + 3 piercing each. Reaction - Cover a Comrade: Add 2 to the AC of one adjacent willing ally against one visible attack, possibly making it miss. This cannot stack with another trooper's use against the same attack.

Tactics and morale: Holds an assigned lane; does not chase a lone PC away from the objective. Surrenders when isolated, lawfully relieved or clearly abandoned. These soldiers are not intended as major damage threats.

Ironfist Shield Warden

Medium combatant. AC 19; HP 85; speed 25 feet. Modifiers: +5, +0, +4, +0, +1, +1. Saves: Strength +8, Constitution +7, Wisdom +4. Perception: +4.

Action - Multiattack: Two hammer attacks, +8 to hit, reach 5 feet; 1d8 + 7 bludgeoning each. Bonus action - Shield Press: After hitting a creature with the hammer this turn, attempt to push it 5 feet or knock it prone; DC 16 Strength save negates. Reaction - Interpose: Reduce damage to one adjacent willing ally by 1d10 + 3, provided the warden sees the attacker.

Tactics and morale: Protects doors, wounded soldiers and records. Two wardens do not fight to the death for a discredited officer when given lawful orders and safe surrender.

Orc Shock Trooper

Medium combatant. AC 17; HP 78; speed 30 feet. Modifiers: +5, +1, +3, +0, +1, +1. Saves: Strength +8, Constitution +6. Perception: +4.

Action - Multiattack: Two heavy axe attacks, +8 to hit, reach 5 feet; 2d8 + 5 slashing each. Bonus action - Press the Line: Move up to 15 feet toward a visible hostile creature; movement provokes normally. If the trooper then hits that creature this turn, the first hit deals an additional 1d6 damage.

Tactics and morale: Clears a route for engineers. Retreats when the mission is impossible and a safe withdrawal exists. The profile can represent an orc, dwarf, goblin or other trained heavy fighter where fiction calls for it.

Goblin Sapper

Small combatant. AC 16; HP 40; speed 30 feet. Modifiers: +0, +4, +2, +3, +1, +0. Saves: Dexterity +7, Intelligence +6. Tools: +6. Stealth: +7.

Action - Multiattack: Two shortblade attacks, +7 to hit, reach 5 feet; 1d6 + 4 piercing each, or one bolt attack, +7 to hit, range 80/320 feet; 1d8 + 4 piercing. Bonus action - Slip Away: Disengage or Hide if the normal circumstances permit hiding.

Action - Thunder Charge, recharge 5-6: Throw a fictional alchemical device to a visible space within 30 feet. At the start of the sapper's next turn it bursts in a 10-foot radius for 3d6 thunder, DC 16 Dexterity save for half. Before then, an adjacent creature can spend an action to throw it to another space within 20 feet or disable it with DC 16 tools. This is a visibly telegraphed fantasy effect, not an unseen trap.

Tactics and morale: Prioritizes controls and sabotage. Abandons a failed mission rather than suicidally detonating among its own civilians. Scene-specific planted charges use that scene's rules, not an additional Thunder Charge countdown.

Tunnel Captain - Brakk and comparable officers

Medium combatant. AC 18; HP 125; speed 30 feet. Modifiers: +4, +2, +3, +1, +2, +2. Saves: Strength +8, Constitution +7, Wisdom +6. Perception: +6.

Action - Multiattack: Three blade attacks, +8 to hit, reach 5 feet; 2d6 + 4 slashing each. Bonus action - Rally, once per encounter: Up to two allies within 30 feet gain 10 temporary HP and can each use their reaction to move 10 feet. Reaction - Punish an Opening: After an adjacent enemy misses the captain with a melee attack, make one blade attack against it.

Tactics and morale: Maintains a route to retreat and tries to preserve specialists. Surrenders if reduced below 25 HP, without effective support, and offered a credible way to survive. A personally fanatical officer may refuse, but establish that before the final blow.

Baldrik Ironfist

Use his existing sheet if one is available. This proposed profile is for rare direct combat or an opposed confrontation; normally he protects a background front and does not take a full extra PC turn every round.

Medium combatant. AC 20; HP 170; speed 25 feet. Modifiers: +5, +1, +4, +0, +2, +2. Saves: Strength +9, Constitution +8, Wisdom +6. Athletics: +9. Perception: +6.

Action - Multiattack: Two warhammer attacks, +9 to hit, reach 5 feet; 2d8 + 5 bludgeoning each. Bonus action - Hold With Me: One willing ally within 10 feet gains advantage on its next attack before the start of Baldrik's next turn. Reaction - The Old Shield: Reduce damage to an adjacent willing ally by 2d8 + 4. Second Wind, once per encounter: As a bonus action, regain 25 HP.

Behaviour: His defensive abilities make protecting someone a visible choice. No feature forces Thorgrinn to trust him or stay close. If he opposes the party, he may surrender, retreat or accept disarmament according to his current convictions.

Marshal-General Hadrik Varr

Medium combatant. AC 20; HP 180; speed 25 feet. Modifiers: +4, +1, +4, +3, +2, +4. Saves: Constitution +8, Wisdom +6, Charisma +8. Insight: +6. Persuasion: +8.

Action - Multiattack: Three command-blade attacks, +9 to hit, reach 5 feet; 2d8 + 4 slashing each. Bonus action - Redeploy: Two willing allies within 30 feet can each use their reaction to move 15 feet. Reaction - Parry: Add 3 AC against one visible melee attack. Legendary actions, 2 per round: Reposition (1): move 15 feet, provoking normally. Strike (2): make one blade attack.

Behaviour: Uses cover, allies and negotiation. Does not acquire immunity to social consequences because he has combat statistics. At 35 HP without loyal support, he offers surrender, evidence or resignation. His political threats cannot magically control a PC.

Korga Emberjaw

Medium combatant. AC 18; HP 220; speed 30 feet. Modifiers: +6, +2, +5, +1, +2, +3. Saves: Strength +10, Constitution +9, Wisdom +6. Athletics: +10. Perception: +6.

Action - Multiattack: Three cleaver attacks, +10 to hit, reach 5 feet; 2d10 + 6 slashing each. Action - Breaking Roar, recharge 5-6: Enemies in a 15-foot cone that can hear him make a DC 17 Wisdom save or are frightened of him until the end of his next turn. Reaction - Brace: Reduce one instance of damage by 1d10 + 5.

Legendary actions, 2 per round: Reposition (1): move up to 15 feet, provoking normally. Cleave (2): make one cleaver attack. Unbroken Will, twice per encounter: When he fails a saving throw, he may succeed instead by taking 20 damage that cannot be reduced. Describe the visible cost so the players know their effect mattered.

Behaviour: Fights to preserve his command and extract concessions. He is capable of surrender; use the concrete conditions in Session 7 rather than a compulsory death speech.

The Bastion Engine

Huge constructed mechanism. AC 19; HP 250; speed 15 feet. Modifiers: +6, -1, +5, -4, +0, -5. Saves: Strength +10, Constitution +9, Wisdom +4. Immune: poison damage, poisoned, charmed, frightened and unconscious. These traits apply to this mindless machine, not automatically to Thorgrinn. No blanket resistance to weapon damage or magic.

Action - Multiattack: Two piston attacks, +10 to hit, reach 15 feet; 3d8 + 7 bludgeoning each. Action - Pressure Burst, recharge 5-6: A clearly visible 20-foot cone; DC 17 Dexterity save, 6d6 force damage, half on success. Legendary actions, 2 per round: Crawl (1): move 10 feet. Piston (2): make one piston attack.

Telegraphed vent hazard: At initiative 20, mark one empty or occupied 20-by-10-foot strip as hissing. At initiative 20 next round it vents for 3d6 fire, DC 16 Dexterity save for half, then a different strip is marked. Never choose every safe route. The warning allows movement, cover and creative interference. This environmental hazard stops when the relief station is complete.

Finale composition: Engine alone is the default guardian. If Hadrik also fights, reduce the engine to 190 HP and remove its legendary actions; give Hadrik his normal profile and no additional guards. An arrested, dead or absent Hadrik does not reappear. Completing all three stations ends the engine's hostile operating state. Destroying it leaves the visible pressure tasks, which the party may resolve without combat opposition.

Shared reward: the Shieldmate's Rivet

An optional original wondrous item, no attunement. One worn rivet or badge, not a separate free copy for every character. Once per long rest, the wearer can use a reaction when a willing ally within 10 feet takes damage to reduce that damage by 1d10 plus the wearer's proficiency bonus. It does not stack with another copy against the same instance. It can be made from a new piece of metal; taking Baldrik's old shield apart requires his and Thorgrinn's consent. The reward represents protection offered, not obedience owed.
